review.notes: The upstream variant's cdb text ('...otherwise you discard 1 random card and look at your opponent's hand.') matches no printed version - it is the modern v4 text (LCYW-EN295) with the era ruling appended, best ratio 0.887 - so the variant pins a ruling, not a printing; hence historical_text_version is taken from the lineage instead: v2 (CP08-EN003, 2009-01-05) is the printing in force across the Edison snapshot, and v0 (SOD-EN056, 2004-10-01) would be the GOAT-era text. Two conflicts preserved rather than resolved: (1) the variant's own appended clause and EdisonFormat both attach the reveal to a FAILED call only, but the script places Duel.ConfirmCards ahead of the branch and reveals unconditionally, and neither models the site's 'publicly accounted-for copies' exemption; (2) the announce filter. Recommendation for escalation: if a reviewer judges the modern announce_filter to be an engine-side declaration convenience rather than an era rules change, this change reduces to the verification procedure alone and should then take date_evidence {kind: shared-chronology, id: search-verification}, under which both GOAT (2005-04-01) and Edison (2010-04-24) sit determinately in the old era. I did not make that call myself, so the change is left with effective {}.

event.historical_text: Declare 1 card name. If that card is in your opponent's hand, they must discard all copies of it in their hand. If it is not, you randomly discard 1 card.
event.summary: Period procedure bundled with a declaration-scope difference, not a text erratum: at resolution the pre-errata script reveals the opponent's entire hand to you (Duel.ConfirmCards(tp,hg)) and then shuffles it (Duel.ShuffleHand(1-tp)), the era's verification procedure for a declared-name call, which the modern script never does; and it declares through an unfiltered Duel.AnnounceCard(tp), so any name including an Extra Deck monster may be called, while the modern script blocks Extra Deck monsters with announce_filter. Chronology is unresolved: the verification element sits inside the shared search-verification bounds, but the declaration-scope element is undated in the packet, so no date evidence is claimed for the change as a whole. Every English lineage text from v0 to v4 is behaviourally identical.
